### README.md (строки 1-182 из 182)
1: # Crazy Putt Arena
2: 
3: Crazy Putt Arena is an original browser-based arcade mini-golf game built with TypeScript, Three.js, Rapier 3D and Vite. The target product is a full match: one human player against configurable bot opponents across themed holes, with mouse aiming, a charged power meter, arcade-tuned ball physics, a scoreboard between holes, and a rating and progression update at the end.
4: 
5: The project is mid-assembly. Most systems are implemented as separate, unit-tested modules under `src/`, but they are not wired into a playable loop yet. Read [Current state](#current-state) first: what `npm run dev` opens today is a menu over an empty 3D scene, not a playable hole.
6: 
7: ## Current state
8: 
9: What happens today when the app runs:
10: 
11: - `src/main.ts` creates a Three.js renderer, an empty scene, a perspective camera and the HTML UI layer above the canvas, then starts a render loop.
12: - `AppUI` (`src/ui/index.ts`) renders the menu and navigates between the main screen, Quick Play / Ranked / Custom setup, Settings and Profile. The profile numbers are placeholder data and the settings form keeps its values in memory only.
13: - **Start Match** reads the setup form and calls an optional `startMatch` callback. `src/main.ts` passes no callbacks, so no match starts.
14: - There is no ball, hole geometry, aiming line, power meter, bot turn, scoreboard or rating update in the browser yet. A production build transforms about 20 modules; the rest of `src/` is not referenced from the entry point.
15: 
16: Implemented and unit-tested, but not reachable from the running page yet:
17: 
18: | Area | Modules |
19: | --- | --- |
20: | ball physics and shots | `src/physics` (`helpers`, `ShotSystem`, `GolfBallPhysics`, `PhysicsWorld`, `CollisionLayers`) |
21: | obstacles | `src/obstacles` (rotating parts, movers, bumper/spring/boost/jump pads, conveyors, fans, teleporters, surface friction) |
22: | hazards and force fields | `src/gameplay/zones` (water, lava, kill, magnet, gravity) |
23: | match flow | `src/gameplay` (`MatchManager`, `TurnManager`, `HoleSystem`, `ScoreManager`, `RatingSystem`, `MatchRewards`, `StateMachine`) |
24: | bots | `src/ai` (`BotPlanner`, `BotProfiles`, `BotTurnScheduler`, `Matchmaking`) |
25: | camera | `src/camera` (controller, modes, smoothing, transitions, collision avoidance) |
26: | courses | `src/courses` and `src/courses/data` (10 courses x 9 holes), `src/core/HoleSceneBuilder` |
27: | player data | `src/player` (profile, progression, cosmetics), `src/core/SaveManager` |
28: | in-game HUD | `src/ui` (`Hud`, `Scoreboard`, `Overlays`, `Minimap`) |
29: 
30: The next step is assembling these in the entry point: build the hole scene, run the physics step, route input into a shot, drive the turn order and mount the HUD.
31: 
32: ## Requirements
33: 
34: - Node.js 20 or newer (checked on 24.8)
35: - A modern desktop browser with WebGL 2 (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari)
36: 
37: ## Install
38: 
39: ```bash
40: npm install
41: ```
42: 
43: ## Run
44: 
45: ```bash
46: npm run dev
47: ```
48: 
49: Vite prints a local URL (http://localhost:5173 by default); open it in the browser. You land on the menu described in [Current state](#current-state).
50: 
51: ## Build
52: 
53: ```bash
54: npm run build
55: ```
56: 
57: The build type-checks the project with `tsc -b` and then emits the bundle into `dist/`.
58: 
59: ## Typecheck
60: 
61: ```bash
62: npm run typecheck
63: ```
64: 
65: ## Test
66: 
67: Two test runners are in use and there is no aggregate `npm test` script yet.
68: 
69: ### Vitest
70: 
71: Vitest covers the suites that sit next to the code in `src/`, plus `tests/course-data-validation.test.ts` (validates 10 courses x 9 holes) and `tests/physics/helpers.test.ts`. The package scripts each run one slice:
72: 
73: ```bash
74: <<<<<<< HEAD
75: npm test
76: ```
77: 
78: `npm test` runs the whole Vitest suite: the colocated unit tests under `src/**` and the
79: cross-module integration tests under `tests/**`. Focused subsets:
80: 
81: ```bash
82: npm run test:ui      # UI layer (src/ui)
83: npm run test:input   # input and developer tools (src/input, src/dev)
84: npm run test:camera  # camera system (src/camera)
85: npm run test:watch   # re-run affected tests on change
86: =======
87: npm run test:ui      # src/ui - 2 files, 11 tests
88: npm run test:input   # src/input and src/dev - 2 files, 5 tests
89: npm run test:camera  # src/camera - 3 files, 32 tests
90: >>>>>>> 87e05bb601a988545be09272d01c792629279b49
91: ```
92: 
93: The whole vitest set runs with:
94: 
95: ```bash
96: npx vitest run
97: ```
98: 
99: Right now 26 files (166 tests) pass and 3 files are reported as failures. All three are runner mismatches rather than broken code:
100: 
101: | File | Why vitest fails on it |
102: | --- | --- |
103: | `tests/leaderboard-generator.test.ts` | written for `node:test`, so vitest reports no test suite found |
104: | `tests/leaderboard-render.test.ts` | same |
105: | `tests/save-manager.test.mjs` | imports from `../.test-build/`, which no script produces |
106: 
107: ### node:test
108: 
109: The two leaderboard suites pass under the Node runner:
110: 
111: ```bash
112: node --test tests/leaderboard-generator.test.ts tests/leaderboard-render.test.ts
113: ```
114: 
115: They import TypeScript sources directly, so Node 22.18+ or 24 is required.
116: 
117: ### Not runnable yet
118: 
119: `tests/save-manager.test.mjs` imports `SaveManager`, the player profile and the progression curve from a compiled `.test-build/` directory. No npm script emits that directory, and a plain `tsc --outDir .test-build` emit is not sufficient because the emitted ESM imports carry no file extensions. Until an emit step (or extension-safe imports) is added, this suite cannot be executed as committed.
120: 
121: ## Project structure
122: 
123: All gameplay code lives under `src/`:
124: 
125: | Folder | Contents |
126: | --- | --- |
127: | `app` | top-level game state shape |
128: | `ai` | bot planners, bot profiles, turn pacing, matchmaking and skill rating |
129: | `assets` | asset and audio managers with graceful fallbacks |
130: | `camera` | camera controller, modes, smoothing and collision avoidance |
131: | `config` | tunable game configuration values |
132: | `contracts` | shared types for events, math, services and zones |
133: | `core` | renderer, scene manager, hole scene builder and save manager |
134: | `courses` | course builder, hole model and the course data sets |
135: | `dev` | launch options, diagnostics overlay and presentation minimap |
136: | `effects` | particle effects |
137: | `gameplay` | match flow, turns, scoring, rating, rewards, state machine and zones |
138: | `input` | keyboard, mouse and touch-ready input handling |
139: | `leaderboard` | leaderboard model, generator and styles |
140: | `obstacles` | rotating parts, movers, pads, conveyors, fans, teleporters, surfaces |
141: | `physics` | physics world, ball physics, shot system and collision layers |
142: | `player` | player profile, progression and ball cosmetics |
143: | `ui` | menu shell, HUD, overlays, scoreboard, minimap and DOM helpers |
144: 
145: Only `config`, `input`, `ui` and (behind the debug flag) `dev` are currently reached from `src/main.ts`.
146: 
147: ## Debug flags
148: 
149: URL flags are parsed by `src/dev/LaunchOptions.ts`:
150: 
151: | Flag | Effect |
152: | --- | --- |
153: | `?debug=1` | lazy-loads `src/dev` and mounts the diagnostics overlay (FPS, frame time, draw calls, triangles, camera position) |
154: | `?course=<id>` | parsed and written to `document.documentElement.dataset.debugCourse`; it does not load the course yet |
155: | `?hole=<n>` | parsed the same way into `dataset.debugHole`; it does not start a hole yet |
156: 
157: Course ids present in `src/courses/data`: `green-hills`, `pirate-bay`, `candy-factory`, `ancient-temple`, `arctic-base`, `volcano`, `neon-city`, `haunted-mansion`, `space-station`, `chaos-dimension`.
158: 
159: Example: `http://localhost:5173/?debug=1&course=volcano&hole=4` shows the overlay and records both values in the DOM dataset. Starting that hole is part of the gameplay loop that is not assembled yet.
160: 
161: Hotkeys, active only while the diagnostics overlay is loaded:
162: 
163: | Key | Effect |
164: | --- | --- |
165: | `F1` | show or hide the diagnostics overlay |
166: | `F2` | toggle wireframe materials on the scene |
167: | `F3` | show or hide the developer presentation minimap (`src/dev/PresentationMinimap.ts`); the in-game minimap in `src/ui/Minimap.ts` is not mounted yet |
168: 
169: ## Audio assets
170: 
171: `public/audio` holds the placeholder structure for sound. No audio binaries are committed: `public/audio/manifest.json` lists every audio event the game can play, using the definition shape consumed by `src/assets/AudioManager.ts` (`id`, `url`, `category`, `volume`, `loop`, `optional`). Every entry is marked optional, so the AudioManager treats a missing file as a non-fatal fallback and the game simply runs silently.
172: 
173: To enable sound, drop `.mp3` files into `public/audio/<category>/<id>.mp3` matching the manifest entries. See `public/audio/README.md` for the folder layout, the entry format and the naming rules.
174: 
175: ## Known gaps
176: 
177: - The entry point does not assemble the gameplay loop: no hole scene, physics step, shot input, turn order or HUD.
178: - `?course` and `?hole` are recorded in the DOM but start nothing.
179: - Menu settings and the profile screen show placeholder data and are not persisted through `SaveManager`.
180: - There is no aggregate test script, and `tests/save-manager.test.mjs` cannot run until its `.test-build/` emit exists.
181: - No audio binaries ship with the repository; the game runs silently by design.
